examples.en: A small diamond is set in the ring.
That diamond is very expensive.
He gave his wife a diamond ring.
It's hard to tell a fake diamond apart.
I saw a necklace made of diamonds.
This watch has diamonds in it too.

explain: '다이아몬드'를 줄인 말이라서 대화에서 편하게 써요. 카드 게임에서 ◆ 모양의 카드도 '다이아'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of 다이아몬드, so it is handy in casual talk. The ◆ suit in card games is also called 다이아.

examples.ko: 동네 쌀집에서 쌀 한 포대를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a sack of rice at the neighborhood rice shop.

examples.ko: 쌀집 아저씨가 쌀을 집까지 배달해 줬어요.
examples.en: The man from the rice shop delivered the rice to my house.
The number of rice shops has dropped a lot these days.

examples.ko: 쌀집에 가면 잡곡도 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go to a rice shop, you can also buy mixed grains.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞에는 오래된 쌀집이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old rice shop in front of my house.
The rice shop sells freshly milled rice.

explain: '쌀가게'도 같은 곳을 가리켜요. '쌀집 아저씨'처럼 가게 주인을 편하게 부를 때도 써요.
explain_en: '쌀가게' refers to the same kind of place. People also use it casually for the owner, as in '쌀집 아저씨'.

examples.en: My monthly income is enough to cover living expenses.
My monthly income is unstable, so I'm worried.
I save about half of my monthly income.
The rent is too expensive compared to my monthly income.
If you add up the couple's monthly income, it's quite comfortable.

examples.ko: 월수입 대비 지출을 매달 적어 봐요.
examples.en: I write down my spending against my monthly income every month.

explain: '월급'은 회사에서 받는 돈이고, '월수입'은 장사나 부업 등을 포함해 한 달에 버는 돈 전체를 말할 수 있어요. 말할 때는 '한 달 수입'이라고도 해요. '월수입이 많다/적다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '월급' is the pay you receive from a company, while '월수입' can include everything you earn in a month, such as business or side jobs. In speech people also say '한 달 수입'. You say '월수입이 많다/적다'.

examples.ko: 이번 달 전기료가 너무 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This month's electricity bill came out really high.

examples.ko: 여름에는 에어컨 때문에 전기료가 두 배로 올라요.
examples.en: In summer the power bill doubles because of the air conditioner.

examples.ko: 전기료를 아끼려고 안 쓰는 플러그를 뽑아요.
examples.en: I unplug things I'm not using to save on the electricity bill.
Do you pay the electricity bill by automatic transfer every month?

examples.ko: 겨울에도 난방 때문에 전기료 걱정이 커요.
examples.en: Even in winter I worry about the power bill because of the heating.
The electricity bill notice came in the mailbox today.

explain: '전기 요금'을 줄인 말이고, 일상에서는 '전기세'라고도 말해요. '전기료가 나오다', '전기료를 내다', '전기료를 아끼다'처럼 '나오다·내다·아끼다'와 자주 같이 써요.
explain_en: It is a short form of '전기 요금', and in daily talk people also say '전기세'. It often goes with verbs like '나오다' (to come out), '내다' (to pay) and '아끼다' (to save), as in '전기료가 나오다'.

examples.en: The bicycle chain came off.
I put the chain on the door and slept.
On snowy roads you put chains on the tires.
I received a chain necklace as a gift.

examples.ko: 이 커피 체인은 전국에 가게가 있어요.
examples.en: This coffee chain has stores all over the country.
The owner of the chain store manages the shop personally.

explain: 자전거 체인처럼 쇠고리를 말하기도 하고, 같은 이름의 가게가 여러 곳에 있는 '체인점'을 말하기도 해요. 가게는 '프랜차이즈'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '체인점'이라고 흔히 말해요.
explain_en: It can mean a metal chain, like a bike chain, or a group of stores under the same name, a '체인점'. Another word for such stores is '프랜차이즈', but '체인점' is the common everyday term.
